name: TEACCH Autism Program
summary: Autism education and clinical training program at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, originator of structured teaching methods used in classrooms and services worldwide.

name: Autism Science Foundation
summary: US nonprofit that funds autism research grants and fellowships and publishes plain-language summaries of autism science for families and clinicians.

name: Autisme Centraal
summary: Flemish training and resource centre in Belgium that educates teachers, care staff and families on autism and publishes practical guidance for schools and workplaces.

name: Gautena
summary: Basque autism association based in San Sebastián providing diagnosis, schooling and vocational training for autistic people across Gipuzkoa province.

name: National Autism Center
summary: US research and training centre, part of the May Institute, that reviews autism intervention evidence and publishes practice guidelines used by schools and clinicians.

name: Autistica
summary: UK autism research charity that funds and commissions studies, sets research priorities with autistic people and families, and campaigns for evidence-based support and services.
notes: States it involves autistic people in setting research priorities.

name: Autism Research Centre, University of Cambridge
summary: University research centre studying the causes and experience of autism across the lifespan, running studies on cognition, biology, and support needs and publishing openly accessible resources.

name: KIND – Center of Neurodevelopmental Disorders at Karolinska Institutet
summary: Karolinska Institutet research and clinical centre in Stockholm studying autism, ADHD and other neurodevelopmental conditions, combining outpatient assessment with academic research programmes.

name: International Dyslexia Association
summary: US-based nonprofit that certifies dyslexia specialists, sets standards for structured literacy instruction, and runs a network of branches supporting people with dyslexia and their families worldwide.

name: Autistic Doctors International
summary: International peer network of autistic physicians and medical students founded by an autistic consultant anaesthetist, supporting members and publishing research on autistic doctors' experiences.
notes: Founder is an autistic physician; group is explicitly by and for autistic doctors.

name: LEPED – Laboratory for Studies and Research in Education and Difference, UNICAMP
name_local: Laboratório de Estudos e Pesquisas em Ensino e Diferença
summary: Research lab at the University of Campinas studying inclusive education for disabled and neurodivergent students, training teachers, and publishing on school inclusion policy in Brazil.

name: Toronto Metropolitan University School of Disability Studies
summary: University department offering disability studies degrees including a Mad Studies stream, taught from a critical, anti-oppressive perspective on disability and psychiatric survivor history.
notes: Formerly Ryerson University.

name: Mad Studies Network
summary: International blog and network connecting scholars, psychiatric survivors and activists working in Mad Studies, sharing calls for papers, syllabi, and writing on madness from a critical, survivor-informed perspective.
notes: Blog/network associated with the Canadian Mad Studies scholarship tradition.

name: Tojisha-Kenkyu Network
name_local: 当事者研究ネットワーク
summary: Japanese network coordinating tojisha-kenkyu, a method in which people with disabilities, mental illness or addiction research and theorize their own experience collaboratively rather than being studied by outsiders.
notes: Tojisha-kenkyu ('research by the person concerned') originated at Bethel House and is associated with researcher Shin'ichiro Kumagaya at the University of Tokyo.

name: PANAACEA
name_local: Programa Argentino para Niños, Adolescentes y Adultos con Condiciones del Espectro Autista
summary: Argentine multi-site research programme studying autism prevalence, early detection and services across the country, coordinating clinicians and researchers with public health institutions.

name: Aspect Research Centre for Autism Practice
summary: Research arm of Autism Spectrum Australia (Aspect) that studies autism education and practice and works to translate findings into classroom and service delivery methods.

name: Limpsfield Grange School
summary: State day and residential special school in Surrey for autistic girls and girls with communication and interaction needs, known for co-authoring books on autistic girls' experience with its students.

name: Ambitious about Autism
summary: UK charity running TreeHouse School and Ambitious College for autistic children and young people, alongside campaigning and information services for autistic students and families.
notes: Founded by parents; runs schools and a college rather than solely campaigning.

name: Fundación CADAH
summary: Spanish online resource and training organisation on ADHD, publishing guidance for families and teachers and running courses on classroom support for children with ADHD.

name: College Autism Network
summary: US network linking researchers, disability service staff and advocates working to improve access and outcomes for autistic students in higher education, publishing research reviews and practice guides.

name: College Internship Program (CIP)
summary: US transition programme with several campuses helping young autistic and ADHD adults build skills for college, employment and independent living through individualized coaching.

name: AHEADD
summary: US organisation coaching college students with autism, ADHD and learning disabilities on academic, social and career skills, and consulting with universities on support services.

name: auticon Germany
summary: German headquarters of auticon, an IT and business consultancy that employs autistic people as consultants and provides workplace coaching and employer training on neuroinclusion.
notes: Founded by Dirk Müller-Remus, whose son is autistic; part of the international auticon network.

name: auticon UK
summary: UK branch of auticon, an IT and business consultancy employing autistic people as consultants and providing neuroinclusion training to client organisations.
notes: Part of the international auticon network.

name: auticon France
summary: French branch of auticon, an IT and business consultancy employing autistic people as consultants and providing neuroinclusion training to client organisations.
notes: Part of the international auticon network.

name: auticon Italy
summary: Italian branch of auticon, an IT and business consultancy employing autistic people as consultants and providing neuroinclusion training to client organisations.
notes: Part of the international auticon network.

name: auticon Switzerland
summary: Swiss branch of auticon, an IT and business consultancy employing autistic people as consultants and providing neuroinclusion training to client organisations.
notes: Part of the international auticon network.

name: auticon Australia
summary: Australian branch of auticon, an IT and business consultancy employing autistic people as consultants and providing neuroinclusion training to client organisations.
notes: Part of the international auticon network.

name: auticon Canada
summary: Canadian branch of auticon, an IT and business consultancy employing autistic people as consultants and providing neuroinclusion training to client organisations.
notes: Part of the international auticon network.

name: auticon Norway
summary: Norwegian branch of auticon, an IT and business consultancy employing autistic people as consultants, formed after auticon acquired Norwegian IT-testing firm Unicus.
notes: unicus.no now redirects to this page.

name: auticon Finland
summary: Finnish branch of auticon, an IT and business consultancy employing autistic people as consultants and providing neuroinclusion training to client organisations.
notes: Part of the international auticon network.

name: Neurodiversity in Business (NiB)
summary: UK charity and membership network helping employers build neuroinclusive workplaces through research, training and a community of practice for HR and diversity professionals.
notes: Formerly at neurodiversityinbusiness.org, which now redirects here.

name: Genius Within
summary: UK community interest company providing coaching, assessment and training for neurodivergent adults in work and job-seeking, and consulting with employers on inclusive practice.
notes: Community interest company; describes services as co-produced drawing on staff lived experience.

name: Exceptional Individuals
summary: UK recruitment and workplace-support agency specialising in placing neurodivergent candidates and providing coaching and access-to-work support once they are hired.

name: Ultranauts
summary: US software quality-engineering company built around a majority-autistic, fully distributed workforce, designing its own management practices around neurodivergent strengths.
notes: Co-founded by an autistic entrepreneur; company describes itself as neurodiversity-led.

name: Rising Tide Car Wash
summary: Florida car wash founded by the family of an autistic young man, employing a majority-autistic workforce and used as a training model shared with other family-run businesses.

name: Aspiritech
summary: Illinois nonprofit social enterprise that trains and employs autistic adults as software testers and quality-assurance analysts for outside clients.

name: Daivergent
summary: US platform that matches autistic and other neurodivergent jobseekers with employers and provides online skills training and job coaching.

name: TAKTO (formerly Passwerk)
summary: Belgian IT consultancy employing autistic professionals as software testers and consultants, rebranded from Passwerk to TAKTO while keeping its autism-employment model.
notes: passwerk.be now redirects to takto.be.

name: Unicus Sweden
summary: Swedish IT-testing consultancy employing autistic consultants, part of a Nordic company model that trains and places autistic professionals with client businesses.
notes: The Norwegian branch (unicus.no) has since become auticon Norway.

name: Neurodiversity Employment Network
summary: Philadelphia-region network connecting employers, service providers and jobseekers to build employment pathways for neurodivergent adults.

name: Yo También
summary: Mexican civil association working on educational and labor inclusion for people with intellectual disabilities, including Down syndrome, through training and workplace-integration programmes.

name: Fundación PRODIS
summary: Madrid foundation providing vocational training and job placement for young people and adults with intellectual disabilities, working with employers on workplace inclusion.

name: The Precisionists Inc.
summary: US IT services company that employs adults with autism and other disabilities as software testers, data analysts and process specialists for corporate clients.

name: DFN Project SEARCH
summary: US national transition-to-employment programme placing young adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities, including autism, in structured workplace internships leading to jobs.
notes: Partnership between the Doug Flutie Jr. Foundation and the Project SEARCH model originated at Cincinnati Children's Hospital.
